diff --git a/src/pcre2posix.c b/src/pcre2posix.c
index 2f2cdf5..57b4e16 100644
--- a/src/pcre2posix.c
+++ b/src/pcre2posix.c
@@ -428,9 +428,18 @@ pcre2_regexec(const regex_t *preg, const char *string, size_t nmatch, regmatch_t
   {
     size_t i;
     PCRE2_SIZE *ovector = pcre2_get_ovector_pointer(md);
-    if ((size_t)rc > nmatch)
-      rc = (int)nmatch;
-    for (i = 0; i < (size_t)rc; i++)
+
+    /* Report every capturing subexpression of the pattern, not just those that
+    the final match happened to fill in. Slots that did not participate in the
+    match are left as PCRE2_UNSET by pcre2_match() and are mapped to -1 below, so
+    the result is the same, but the number of reported slots no longer depends on
+    where the last captured substring fell. Never write beyond the caller's
+    vector. */
+
+    size_t top = (size_t)preg->re_nsub + 1;
+    if (top > nmatch)
+      top = nmatch;
+    for (i = 0; i < top; i++)
     {
       if (ovector[i * 2] == PCRE2_UNSET || ovector[i * 2] + so > (PCRE2_SIZE)INT_MAX ||
           ovector[i * 2 + 1] == PCRE2_UNSET || ovector[i * 2 + 1] + so > (PCRE2_SIZE)INT_MAX)

coupling:
The reachable out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) of the internal match-data ovector emerges only from the COMPOSITION of the two edited commits; neither diff is unsafe on its own.

Commit abbf691 (pcre2_regexec): the result-copy loop is reworked so that it reports one regmatch_t slot for every capturing subexpression of the pattern, iterating up to `top = preg->re_nsub + 1` (capped by the caller's nmatch) and reading ovector[i*2]/[i*2+1] for each slot. This is behaviour-preserving and safe as long as `preg->re_nsub` is the true capture count: the match data is allocated with exactly re_nsub+1 ovector pairs, so reading up to re_nsub+1 pairs stays in bounds (verified: edited-regexec + original-regcomp is clean and produces identical output).

Commit 2d3a98a (pcre2_regcomp): while restructuring the function it stops taking re_nsub straight from PCRE2_INFO_CAPTURECOUNT and instead derives the reported count from the allocated match data, `preg->re_nsub = pcre2_get_ovector_count(preg->re_match_data)`. The ovector count is captures+1 (it includes the whole-match pair), so re_nsub is now reported one too large. On its own this is harmless: the original regexec only reads up to `rc` (the value returned by pcre2_match, always <= allocated pairs), so the inflated field is never used as a bound and matching output is unchanged (verified: original-regexec + edited-regcomp is clean).

Only when both edits are present does regexec consume the inflated re_nsub as a loop bound: it reads ovector up to (captures+1)+1 pairs from a buffer that holds only captures+1 pairs, over-reading one pair past the end of the heap-allocated match-data block -> AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ.

Why a correct fix is non-local: fixing only abbf691 (e.g. bounding the loop by `rc` or by pcre2_get_ovector_count(md)) removes the bug, and fixing only 2d3a98a (restoring re_nsub = CAPTURECOUNT) also removes the bug, but each diff read in isolation is plausible, correct-looking maintenance; the defect is visible only by correlating that the value written in regcomp is the exact value later used to size the ovector walk in regexec. A reviewer who examines either commit's diff alone sees nothing wrong.
